examples: She checked her baggage at the airport counter before boarding the flight.
او چمدانش را قبل از سوار شدن به هواپیما در باجه فرودگاه تحویل داد.
Airlines often charge extra fees for heavy baggage.
خطوط هوایی اغلب برای چمدان‌های سنگین هزینه اضافی دریافت می‌کنند.
After years of a difficult marriage, he carried a lot of emotional baggage into his next relationship.
پس از سال‌ها یک ازدواج سخت، او بار عاطفی زیادی را وارد رابطه بعدی‌اش کرد.
miniContext: At the airport, baggage can be the biggest source of stress before a flight. Passengers line up to check their baggage, hoping it will not be too heavy or arrive late. Beyond travel, people also talk about emotional baggage — the worries and memories from the past that we carry into new situations. Understanding both senses of baggage helps explain why the word appears so often in everyday conversation.

examples: The flood was the worst calamity the small town had ever experienced.
آن سیل بدترین مصیبتی بود که آن شهر کوچک تا به حال تجربه کرده بود.
Losing both his job and his home in the same month felt like a personal calamity.
از دست دادن شغل و خانه‌اش در یک ماه برایش مثل یک فاجعه شخصی بود.
Historians still study how the empire recovered from that calamity.
تاریخ‌نگاران هنوز بررسی می‌کنند که آن امپراتوری چگونه از آن فاجعه جان سالم به در برد.
miniContext: A calamity is an event so destructive that it changes the course of people's lives. Earthquakes, floods, and wars are often described as calamities because of the widespread suffering they cause. Sometimes the word is also used more personally, for a single event that feels catastrophic to one person, like losing a job or a home. Whether large or small in scale, a calamity leaves lasting damage behind it.

examples: He died a pauper after losing his entire fortune in bad investments.
او پس از از دست دادن تمام ثروتش در سرمایه‌گذاری‌های نادرست، به عنوان یک فقیر تهیدست از دنیا رفت.
The old hospital once buried unidentified paupers in a shared grave.
آن بیمارستان قدیمی زمانی افراد فقیر تهیدست ناشناس را در یک گور دسته‌جمعی دفن می‌کرد.
In the novel, the prince trades places with a pauper for a day.
در آن رمان، شاهزاده برای یک روز جایش را با یک فقیر تهیدست عوض می‌کند.
miniContext: A pauper is someone with almost no money or possessions, often dependent on charity to survive. In earlier centuries, paupers who died without family were sometimes buried in unmarked public graves. The word appears frequently in classic literature, where a wealthy character disguises himself as a pauper to see how the poor are truly treated. Today the term sounds old-fashioned, but it still captures the extreme end of poverty.

examples: Engineers warned that the old bridge could collapse if it carried any more traffic.
مهندسان هشدار داده بودند که اگر پل قدیمی ترافیک بیشتری را تحمل کند، ممکن است فرو بریزد.
The company's stock price collapsed after the scandal was revealed.
قیمت سهام شرکت پس از افشای آن رسوایی سقوط کرد.
She felt so exhausted that she nearly collapsed at the finish line.
او آنقدر خسته بود که نزدیک بود در خط پایان از پا بیفتد.
miniContext: A structure, a system, or even a person can collapse when it suddenly gives way under too much pressure. Bridges and buildings collapse when their materials can no longer support the weight placed on them, while economies collapse when confidence and money disappear too quickly. The word also describes a person falling down suddenly from exhaustion or illness. In every case, collapse suggests a sudden, often dramatic failure rather than a slow decline.

examples: The architect designed a house with large windows to let in natural light.
آن معمار خانه‌ای با پنجره‌های بزرگ طراحی کرد تا نور طبیعی وارد شود.
She studied for seven years before she was licensed as an architect.
او هفت سال تحصیل کرد تا پیش از آنکه به عنوان معمار مجوز بگیرد.
Historians consider him the chief architect of the country's new constitution.
تاریخ‌نگاران او را معمار اصلی قانون اساسی جدید آن کشور می‌دانند.
miniContext: An architect plans and designs buildings, balancing beauty, safety, and function. Before any construction begins, the architect draws detailed plans that engineers and builders follow closely. The word is also used figuratively for anyone who carefully designs a plan or system, such as the architect of a peace treaty or a new policy. In both senses, an architect is responsible for shaping something complex from the ground up.

examples: The district attorney decided to prosecute the suspect for fraud.
دادستان ناحیه تصمیم گرفت آن متهم را به دلیل کلاهبرداری تحت پیگرد قضایی قرار دهد.
Without enough evidence, prosecutors could not prosecute the case in court.
بدون شواهد کافی، دادستان‌ها نتوانستند آن پرونده را در دادگاه پیگیری کنند.
The government vowed to prosecute anyone involved in the corruption scandal.
دولت متعهد شد که هر کسی را که در آن رسوایی فساد دخیل بود، تحت پیگرد قضایی قرار دهد.
miniContext: To prosecute someone means to formally charge them with a crime and pursue the case against them in court. A prosecutor must gather enough evidence before deciding to prosecute, since a weak case can collapse before a judge. News reports often describe officials vowing to prosecute corruption or fraud to reassure the public that justice will be served. The word belongs mainly to legal and criminal contexts.

examples: He managed to squander his entire inheritance on gambling within two years.
او موفق شد کل ارث خود را در عرض دو سال در قمار هدر دهد.
Don't squander this opportunity; it may never come again.
این فرصت را هدر نده؛ ممکن است دیگر هیچ‌وقت تکرار نشود.
The team squandered a two-goal lead in the final ten minutes.
آن تیم برتری دو گله‌اش را در ده دقیقه پایانی از دست داد.
miniContext: To squander something means to waste it carelessly, especially money, time, or a valuable opportunity. People squander fortunes through reckless spending, and athletes sometimes squander a comfortable lead through poor decisions near the end of a match. The word carries a tone of regret, suggesting that what was lost could easily have been kept with more care. It is most often paired with resources that cannot be recovered once gone.

examples: Police searched the forest for the fugitive who had escaped from prison.
پلیس جنگل را برای یافتن آن فراری که از زندان گریخته بود، جست‌وجو کرد.
The fugitive was finally captured after three weeks on the run.
آن فراری سرانجام پس از سه هفته فرار، دستگیر شد.
She lived as a fugitive for years, moving from city to city to avoid arrest.
او سال‌ها به عنوان یک فراری زندگی کرد و برای فرار از دستگیری از شهری به شهر دیگر می‌رفت.
miniContext: A fugitive is someone running away from the law, usually after escaping custody or avoiding arrest. News reports often describe a massive manhunt as police try to track down a dangerous fugitive before they can leave the country. The word can also describe someone fleeing persecution rather than punishment, such as a political fugitive seeking asylum abroad. In every case, the defining feature of a fugitive is the act of fleeing.

examples: He was arrested for bigamy after marrying a second wife without divorcing the first.
او به دلیل دوهمسری غیرقانونی، پس از ازدواج با همسر دومش بدون طلاق گرفتن از همسر اولش، بازداشت شد.
Bigamy is illegal in most countries, even if both marriages were entered willingly.
دوهمسری غیرقانونی در بیشتر کشورها جرم محسوب می‌شود، حتی اگر هر دو ازدواج با رضایت طرفین انجام شده باشد.
The court found her guilty of bigamy and annulled the second marriage.
دادگاه او را به دوهمسری غیرقانونی محکوم کرد و ازدواج دوم را باطل اعلام کرد.
miniContext: Bigamy is the crime of marrying someone while still legally married to another person. Most legal systems treat bigamy as a serious offense because it violates the terms of the first marriage contract without ending it. Cases of bigamy sometimes come to light only when one spouse discovers the other's hidden marriage years later. Because it combines fraud with family law, bigamy often leads to both criminal charges and the annulment of the second marriage.

examples: She decided to study abroad for her final year of university.
او تصمیم گرفت سال آخر دانشگاهش را در خارج از کشور تحصیل کند.
Many young professionals move abroad to find better job opportunities.
بسیاری از متخصصان جوان برای یافتن فرصت‌های شغلی بهتر به خارج از کشور مهاجرت می‌کنند.
News of the scandal quickly spread abroad, damaging the company's reputation worldwide.
خبر آن رسوایی به سرعت به خارج از کشور رسید و به اعتبار جهانی شرکت آسیب زد.
miniContext: Abroad means in or to a foreign country, away from one's home nation. Students often choose to study abroad to experience a new culture and improve their language skills, while workers may move abroad for better career prospects. The word can also describe how news or ideas travel outside a country's borders, spreading abroad until they become known internationally. In everyday speech, abroad simply contrasts with staying at home.

examples: She couldn't help feeling envy when her coworker got the promotion she wanted.
او نتوانست از حسادت کردن به همکارش که آن ترفیعی را که خودش می‌خواست گرفت، خودداری کند.
His new car was the envy of the whole neighborhood.
ماشین جدیدش حسادت کل محله را برانگیخته بود.
Try not to envy others' success; focus on your own goals instead.
سعی کن به موفقیت دیگران حسادت نکنی؛ در عوض روی اهداف خودت تمرکز کن.
miniContext: Envy is the uncomfortable feeling of wanting what someone else has, whether it is their success, their possessions, or their relationships. People often feel envy toward coworkers, friends, or even siblings when comparing their own lives unfavorably. The phrase "the envy of" describes something so desirable that others wish they had it too. Although envy is a natural emotion, letting it grow can damage friendships and create constant dissatisfaction.

examples: The couple entered into matrimony after a long engagement.
آن زوج پس از نامزدی طولانی، ازدواج کردند.
The priest spoke about the sacred bond of matrimony during the ceremony.
کشیش در طول مراسم درباره پیوند مقدس ازدواج سخن گفت.
They have been happily living in matrimony for over thirty years.
آن‌ها بیش از سی سال است که با خوشحالی در پیوند ازدواج زندگی می‌کنند.
miniContext: Matrimony is a formal word for marriage, often used in religious or legal ceremonies. Wedding vows frequently mention the sacred bond of matrimony, emphasizing commitment and lifelong partnership. The word appears more often in traditional or ceremonial contexts than in casual conversation, where people simply say marriage. Still, matrimony carries a certain formality that suits official documents and wedding speeches alike.
